Christ came into the world not so that he might be served, but so that he himself might serve others. Matt. 20. Antichrist, therefore, will be whoever under the pretext of Christ demands the services of all, and seeks to lord it over all. Christ humbled himself to such lowliness that he washed the feet of his disciples. Antichrist, therefore, cannot but be the one who offers his feet to be kissed by the professors of the Christian name, and even by kings. Christ refused to take up the crown of the kingdom when it was offered. Antichrist, therefore, is whoever under the false name of Christ claims for himself the crowns of kingdoms. Christ was always occupied with the salvation of his flock. Antichrist, therefore, is he who, professing himself the shepherd of the Christian flock, attends rather to private advantage and to the gathering of wealth than to the salvation of the faithful. Christ cast out of the temple those who sold and bought. Antichrist, therefore, is whoever brings those same men back into the temples, and makes the Church a market-house. Christ frees his own from the bondage of the law. Antichrist imposes intolerable burdens of human traditions. Christ willed that marriages be free, and recalled them to their first institution. Antichrist, therefore, is he who takes away their freedom and forbids them as if they were impure. Christ abolished the distinctions of foods. Antichrist, therefore, will be whoever brings them back. The kingdom of Christ is not of this world, nor is it acquired and preserved by worldly arms. We rightly call him truly Antichrist, therefore, whoever, pretending Christ, aspires to the kingdoms of the world, and acquires and retains them by arms. In short, whatever is discerned in the doctrine and life of Christ, its contrary may be found in Antichrist.

units.la: Alterum Antichristi epitheton est, quod illum supra Deum eleuatum iri Paulus dicit, quod non aliud est, quam sibi vendicare quae solius Dei sunt. Solius Dei est sanctum esse & sanctifica-re alios: quare ab angelis illi acclamatur, Sanctus, sanctus, sanctus dominus exercituum. Isa.6. Et 6.Et ipse apud prophetam se eum esse profitetur, qui Israelem sanctificet. Ezech.37. Solius Dei est, peccata remittere, eo quod soli Deo peccatur: quod & pharisei, vtcunque aliās caeci, agnoscere potuerunt. Marci 2. Solius Dei est, iudicia habere inscrutabilia & vias imperuestigabiles, nec vlli hominum reprehensioni subiacere. Solus Deus vel nouas res creare, vel creaturas mutare & transsubstantiare potest. Quisquis ergo se patrem sanctum, vel ipsam sanctitatem appellari vult: quisquis peccatorum remissionem sui priuati iuris esse contendit: quisquis in sua facta & consilia inuestigari prohibet, seque per omnia irreprehensibilem esse superbe gloriatur: quisquis denique nouas Creaturas formare, & substantias rerum in alias se mutare posse, arroganter iactat, is supra Deum sese effert, & cum Lucifero thronum suum ponit in nubibus coeli, cum eodem in-de deturbandus in stagnum ardens igne & sulphure. Haec si hodie inquiras & examines, Antichristus quis sit, facile inuenies. Nec, vt eum e Babylone oriturū expectemus, opus est. In ipsae-nim ecclesia Christi iam aliquot seculis sederunt, quorum doctrina & vitae institutum cū Christo pugnare constat. In eadem hodie inueniuntur, qui sanctitatis titulum sibi vendicant: qui pro-pria authoritate quos libet sanctificant, imo in diuos referunt: qui penes se esse contendunt, pec-cata vel retinere vel dimittere: qui se à nemine accusari debere clamat, etiamsi cateruatim animas hominum primo gehennae mancipio excruciandas demiserint: qui denique rerum substantias vi verborū, quae ipsi proferunt, se couertere posse iactitant. Si quis ergo hos Antichristos esse negauerit, is & solem lucis authore esse, negare audebit. Sed quia multa in hos scripta publice extant, & nos alibi hoc negotium prolixe tractauimus, paucula haec modo sufficiant. Illud tamen fideles cogitent, nō leue esse, quod ab Antichristo imminet periculum, nec verborum pugnas esse, quae contra hunc dicuntur. Agitur enim hic de Christi gloria, quae pijs omnibus commendatissima esse debet. Agitur de animarum salute, quam nos omni studio quaerere, & inuentam retinere conuenit. Et cum de hoc olim tanta diligentia spiritus sanctus admonuerit, nos sua tyrannide grassantem & insolenter elatum, digito monstremus, alta & libera voce prodamus, ne quis nostra incuria in illius manus nefarias delapsus, vitae iacturā faciat. Excitet nos Christi exemplum, & Ioannis dilecti illius discipuli industria, qui de membris Antichristi sic dicere pergit.
units.tr: The second epithet of Antichrist is that Paul says he will be lifted up above God, which is nothing other than claiming for himself what belongs to God alone. It belongs to God alone to be holy and to make others holy; therefore the angels acclaim him: "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts," Isa. 6. And in the prophet he himself professes to be the one who sanctifies Israel, Ezek. 37. It belongs to God alone to forgive sins, since sin is committed against God alone; the Pharisees, blind as they were in other respects, were able to acknowledge this, Mark 2. It belongs to God alone to have unsearchable judgments and inscrutable ways, and to be subject to no human reprehension. God alone can create new things, or change and transubstantiate creatures. Whoever therefore wishes to be called a holy father, or holiness itself; whoever contends that the forgiveness of sins is in his own private right; whoever forbids his deeds and counsels to be investigated, and proudly boasts that he is blameless in all things; whoever, finally, arrogantly claims that he can form new creatures and change the substances of things into others, he exalts himself above God, and sets his throne with Lucifer in the clouds of heaven, to be cast down with him into the burning lake of fire and sulphur. If you inquire into and examine these things today, you will easily discover who Antichrist is. Nor do we need to wait for him to come out of Babylon. For they have sat in the very Church of Christ for several centuries now, whose teaching and way of life are plainly at odds with Christ. The same men are found today who claim for themselves the title of holiness; who on their own authority sanctify whomever they please, and even raise them to the rank of gods; who contend that the power to retain or to forgive sins lies with them; who cry out that no one ought to accuse them, even though they have sent souls of men by the crowd to be tortured first in the servitude of hell; who finally boast that they can convert the substances of things by the force of the words they utter. If anyone therefore denies that these are Antichrists, he will dare to deny that the sun is the author of light. But since many writings on these men are publicly extant, and we have treated this matter at length elsewhere, let these few remarks suffice for now. Yet let the faithful consider that the danger hanging over us from Antichrist is no light matter, nor are the battles of words waged against him empty. For here the glory of Christ is at stake, which ought to be commended most highly to all the godly. The salvation of souls is at stake, which we should seek with all zeal and, once found, hold fast. And since the Holy Spirit long ago gave such careful warning about this, let us point with our finger at him who rages with his tyranny and proudly exalts himself, and let us proclaim it with a loud and free voice, lest anyone, through our carelessness, fall into his nefarious hands and suffer the loss of life. Let the example of Christ and the diligence of John, that beloved disciple, stir us up, for he goes on to speak thus of the members of Antichrist.

units.la: I I. E nobis egressi sunt, sed non erant ex nobis. Nam si fuissent ex nobis, permansissent utique nobiscum. Sed ut manifesti fierent, quod non sint omnes ex nobis. Unde seductores & Antichristiani spiritus prodeant docet, vt intelligamus, à quibus periculum maximè timendum sit: simul autem offen-diculis medetur, quae hic grauissima obiici solent. Cum enim doctrinae Christi hostes esse videmus, & pestilentissimorum dogmatum authores, qui & Christi nomine gloriantur, & huius prae-textu traditiones suas ecclesijs obtrudere student, uariae in animis nostris cogitationes exurgut. Aut enim de doctrinae Christi veritate dubitamus, cū illam in tot tamque diuersas haereses scin-di cernimus, quae singulae huius authoritate niti videri volunt: aut Christum putamus de regno suo non vehementer solicitum esse, eo quod sub fui nominis praetextu ista fieri permittat. Sed omnibus hisce Ioannes respondet dicens: E nobis egresi sunt, sed non erant ex nobis. Non est (inquit) quod horum peruerfitate aliquis moueatur, quasi doctrinae Christi ambigua & incerta praedicatio tales fecerit. Licet enim e nobis, id est, externo ecclesiae coetu prodierint, cuius membra hucusque videri voluerunt: e nobis tamen minimè fuerunt. Nec enim Christum vnquam vera fide amplexi sunt, nec veritatis cognitioni studuerunt, nec salutis viam inquisiuerunt, sed vel priuati commodi, vel licentiae carnalis causa Christianos sese ad tempus simulauerunt. Nam si vere ex nobis, id est, vera Christi & ecclesiae ipsius membra, ac verae gregis Christi oues fuissent, nunquam à nobis fuissent auulsi, sed permansissent in nostra communione firmiter, cum oues Christi nemo de sua manu rapere, nec fideles aliquis à Dei dilectione separare posit. Ioan.10. Rom. 8.Indignū ergo est, Christo & doctrinae ipsius imputare eorū culpam, quos Christi cultores & doctrinae ipsius sectatores nunquam fuisse constat. Iniquum item, nobis illorum peruerfitatem exprobrare, qui ecclesiae nostrae membra nunquam fuerunt, sed externa tantummodo conuersatione priuatas ob causas ad tempus nobiscum vsi sunt. Sed & ipse Deus ecclesiae suae consultum cupiens, spiritum vertiginis illis immittit, vt palam ab ecclesia deficiant, illius communionem deferant, doctrinam ecclesiæ oppugnent, & noua atq; portentosa dogmata ferant, quò omnibus constet, illos nunquâ ex ouiû & fidelium suorû numero fuisse, nec ecclesiæ imputari debere, si quid ab his perperam factum fuerit. Vtinam hæc ab ijs expenderentur diligétius, qui nobis hodie Anabaptistarum intemperiem acceptam ferunt, & euangelij doctrinæ fructus esse clamitant, quòd ab ecclesia secessionem faciunt, quòd magistratui debitam obedientiam negant, quòd cõiugijs promiscuis quidam vtuntur, quòd rerum omniû cõmunionem inuehere student, & alia multa cõminiscuntur, quæ & rempub. & ecclesiam mirificè & perniciosè turbât. Atqui Anabaptistas ex illorum grege & numero ferè prodire, qui euangeliû Christi profitentur, nõ negamus. Sed reuera euágelij studiosos & veras Christi oues fuisse, nunquâ cõcedemus: minus vero admittemus, illos insana hæc & absurda figmëta ex euágelio hausisse. Si enim ex nobis fuissent, mansissent vtiq; nobiscum, nec vnquâ ab ecclesia secessionem facerent, nec eorû authores essent, quæ cû Christi doctrina manifestè pugnant. Insunt autem huic loco & alia quædã, de quibus propter insignem nostri seculi corruptionem sigillatim aliquid dicendum erit.
units.tr: 1 John 2. They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us. But that they might be made manifest, that not all are of us. Here he teaches whence seducers and the spirit of Antichrist come forth, so that we may understand from whom the danger is to be feared most; at the same time he remedies the stumbling blocks that are commonly raised here as the most serious. For when we see enemies of the teaching of Christ, and authors of the most pestilent dogmas, who both glory in the name of Christ and under that pretext strive to impose their own traditions upon the churches, various thoughts arise in our minds. For either we doubt the truth of Christ's teaching, since we see it split into so many and such diverse heresies, each of which wishes to appear to rest on its authority; or we think that Christ is not greatly concerned for his kingdom, since he permits these things to happen under the pretext of his name. But John answers all these things, saying: "They went out from us, but they were not of us." There is no reason (he says) for anyone to be moved by their perversity, as if the uncertain and doubtful preaching of Christ's teaching had produced such men. For although they went out from us, that is, from the external assembly of the Church, whose members they wished until now to appear, yet they were by no means of us. For they never embraced Christ with true faith, nor did they strive for knowledge of the truth, nor did they seek the way of salvation; but for the sake of private advantage or carnal licence they pretended for a time to be Christians. For if they had truly been of us, that is, true members of Christ and of the Church itself, and true sheep of Christ's flock, they would never have been torn away from us, but would have remained firmly in our communion, since no one can snatch Christ's sheep from his hand, nor can anyone separate the faithful from the love of God. John 10; Rom. 8. It is therefore unworthy to impute to Christ and to his teaching the guilt of those who were never worshippers of Christ and followers of his teaching. It is likewise unfair to reproach us with the perversity of those who were never members of our Church, but only for private reasons associated with us for a time by external conduct. But God himself, desiring the good of his Church, sends upon them a spirit of giddiness, so that they openly fall away from the Church, forsake its communion, attack the teaching of the Church, and bring forth new and monstrous dogmas; so that it may be clear to all that they were never of the number of the sheep and of his faithful, and that if anything has been done amiss by them, it ought not to be imputed to the Church. Would that these things were weighed more carefully by those who today lay the disorder of the Anabaptists at our door, and cry out that it is a fruit of the doctrine of the gospel, because they secede from the Church, because they deny due obedience to the magistrate, because some of them practise promiscuous marriages, because they strive to introduce a community of all goods, and devise many other things which disturb both the commonwealth and the Church in a wonderful and pernicious way. Yet we do not deny that the Anabaptists come for the most part from the flock and number of those who profess the gospel of Christ. But we shall never concede that they were true lovers of the gospel and true sheep of Christ; and still less shall we admit that they drew these mad and absurd fictions from the gospel. For if they had been of us, they would surely have remained with us, nor would they ever have seceded from the Church, nor would they be the authors of things that clearly fight against the teaching of Christ. There are, moreover, other matters contained in this passage, on which, because of the notable corruption of our age, something must be said separately.

units.la: Primò obseruandũ venit, vnde ecclesiæ Christi grauissimi & nocentissimi hostes exurgant, Ex ipsa nimirû ecclesia, & illorum numero, qui & ecclesia & primi illius antistites haberi volunt. Nisi enim tales se esse simularent, nunquam ab ecclesia admitterentur. Exempla infinita sunt in veteri testamento, vbi sanctis Dei prophetis semper cum illis plurimum negotij fuisse legimus, qui & ipsi prophetæ dici volebant, & spiritu prophetico gloriabantur, & reuelationes diuinas ia ëtitabát[?]. Sed in Iuda hoc ipsum egregiè figuratum & adumbratum habemus, qui cum ex numero duodecim Christi discipulorum esset, Christi hostis & proditor fieri voluit. Similiter & Nazaræi, qui Apostolorû temporibus iustitiam legis vrgebant, nequaquâ à Christo alieni videri volebát, sed Paulum potius accusabant, quòd minus legitimè Apostoli munus suscepisset. Quód si vaticinia Apostolorum de nouissimi seculi impostoribus consyderes, in ipsa ecclesia illos monstrari videbis. Et de magno illo Antichristo, omnis impietatis capite, Paulus diserte testatur, quòd in templo Dei sedem suam habituru sit. 2. Thess. 2. Nemo igitur vel à Turcis vel à Iudæis sibi tantum timeat, quantum ex domesticis nostræ fidei hostibus. Nemo Antichristû è Babylone & tribu Dan oriundum expectet, sed ab eo sibi caueant omnes, qui in ecclesia Christi, in vrbe olim rerum domina, super septem montes sedens, calice fornicationum suarû iam aliquot seculis reges & gentes inebriatas dementauit, &c. vide Apoc. 17.
units.tr: First, it must be observed whence the most grievous and most harmful enemies of the Church of Christ arise: namely, from the Church itself, and from the number of those who wish to be regarded as the Church and its first leaders. For unless they pretended to be such, they would never be admitted by the Church. There are countless examples in the Old Testament, where we read that the holy prophets always had very much trouble with those who wished themselves to be called prophets, and gloried in the prophetic spirit, and boasted of divine revelations. But in Judas we have this very thing excellently foreshadowed and prefigured: he, although he was of the number of the twelve disciples of Christ, wished to become an enemy and betrayer of Christ. Likewise the Nazarenes, who in the times of the apostles insisted on the righteousness of the law, were by no means willing to seem alien to Christ, but rather accused Paul, because he had assumed the office of apostle less lawfully. But if you consider the prophecies of the apostles concerning the impostors of the last age, you will see that they are shown to arise within the Church itself. And concerning that great Antichrist, the head of all impiety, Paul plainly testifies that he will set up his seat in the temple of God, 2 Thess. 2. Let no one therefore fear the Turks or the Jews as much as the domestic enemies of our faith. Let no one expect Antichrist to come from Babylon and the tribe of Dan; rather let all beware of him who, in the Church of Christ, sitting in the city once mistress of the nations, upon seven hills, has for several centuries now made kings and peoples drunk and mad with the cup of her fornications, etc. See Rev. 17.

units.la: Secundò signum & notam proponit Apostolus, ex qua Antichristiani doctores agnosci possint, quæ est, quòd exeunt ab ecclesia, non autem vera sunt ecclesiæ membra, vtcunq; titulo Christi & fidei glorientur, nec cum fidelibus permanent, id est, nõ perseuerant in doctrina & fide, quâ Christi ecclesia amplectitur, & ab ipso Christo traditam agnoscit. Quotquot enim oues Christi sunt, Christi vocem audiunt. Ioan. 10. Quotquot item fideles Christi & ecclesiæ ministri sunt, nõ alienam vocem afferunt, non nouis dogmatibus ecclesiam aggrauant, nõ sibi ipsis discipulos demerentur, non scindunt ecclesiæ vnitatem: sed auditores suos omnes ad vnum Christû relegant, huic discipulos faciunt, & iuxta præceptum Christi ea illos seruare docet, quæ ipse olim viua voce tradidit, & ab Apostolis spiritus suggestione literis mandata sunt. Cum enim ex Apostolorum numero nemo tantum sibi arrogare ausus fit, vt nouum euangelium prædicare, Apostolico spiritu nunquam præditos putabimus, quicunq; id hodie tentant, nec cum reliquis fidelibus in simplici Christi doctrina & fidei vnitate permanent. Verè ergo Ioannes inquit: Si ex nobis essent, si verè Christiani & fideles Christi ministri essent, permansissent vtiq; nobiscum. Debet sententia hæc omnibus hæreticis, qui olim ecclesiam turbarunt, accommodari. Si ex fidelium numero fuisset Arrius, Christi diuinitatem, quæ à fidelibus constanter creditur, nunquam negauisset, sed in eadem cum alijs fidelibus confessione permansisset. Si ex Christi ouibus fuissent Martionitæ, permansissent vtique in vnanimi ecclesiæ doctrina & fide, quæ verâ Christi humanitate agnoscit, & phantastici corporis figmentum ignorat. Id quia non fecerunt, veros Christi fideles nõ fuisse cõstat. Eadem de illis dici debent, qui hodie euangelij doctrinâ negare audent. Nec enim iuuabit Pontificios, quòd Christû profitentur, quòd sub Christi prætextu sua omnia obtrudunt, quòd Apostolorû successione gloriantur. Si enim ex nobis, id est, ex vero Christi grege essent, nobiscum utique permanerent, nec ab Apostolorû doctrina, quæ sola fide in Christû absque operibus legis nos iustificari docet, recederent. Quia verò humanarû traditionû operibus tribuere audent, quod operibus legis diuinitus traditæ Apostoli cõstanter negarunt, ex Apostolis & horû legitimis successoribus esse nõ possunt. Similiter, si ex Christi fidelibus essent, nobiscum in ea fide & doctrina permaneret, quæ Christû Iesum vnicum mediatorem inter Deû & homines esse tradit, nec ab ea declinantes nouos & innumeros mediatores fingerent. Si ex Christi ecclesia essent, Christi testamentum, quod in vltima Coena ipse instituit, minimè peruerterent, sed commemorationem esse agnoscerent mortis domini, non sacrificij per Christum oblati iterationem comminiscerentur. Si ex Christi grege essent, solius Christi vocem audirent, nec humanas traditiones, tam graui Christi sententia damnatas, ecclesiæ multum reclamanti obtruderent. Denique, si Christi spiritu ducerentur, in ijs permanerent constanti fide, quæ per Christum nobis tradita sunt, & anathema ducerent eum, qui nouum euangelium, nouam fidem, nouam salutis rationem docere præsumeret, siue is Apostolus esset, siue angelus coelo delapsus, Gal.1. Hoc quia non faciunt, sed Patres, Concilia, Canones & alia quædam huius farinæ prætexunt, ex illorum numero, quorum authoritate nituntur, illos esse fatebimur: sed ex grege fidelium Christi illos esse nunquam agnoscemus. Si enim ex nobis essent, permanerent vtique nobiscum.
units.tr: Secondly, the Apostle sets out a sign and mark by which Antichristian teachers may be recognised: that they go out from the Church and are not true members of it, however much they may boast of the title of Christ and of the faith, and that they do not remain with the faithful, that is, they do not persist in the teaching and faith which the Church of Christ embraces and acknowledges as handed down by Christ himself. For all who are Christ's sheep hear Christ's voice. John 10. Likewise, all who are faithful to Christ and are ministers of the Church do not bring forward a strange voice, do not burden the Church with new doctrines, do not win disciples for themselves, do not rend the unity of the Church; rather they refer all their hearers to the one Christ, make disciples for him, and teach them, according to Christ's command, to observe those things which he himself once delivered by the living voice, and which were committed to writing by the Apostles under the prompting of the Spirit. For since no one from the number of the Apostles dared to claim for himself the right to preach a new gospel, we shall judge that those who today attempt this, and do not remain with the rest of the faithful in the simple doctrine of Christ and the unity of the faith, are never endowed with the Apostolic spirit. Truly, then, John says: "If they had been of us, if they had truly been Christians and faithful ministers of Christ, they would surely have remained with us." This saying ought to be applied to all the heretics who in former times troubled the Church. If Arius had been of the number of the faithful, he would never have denied the divinity of Christ, which is constantly believed by the faithful, but would have remained in the same confession as the other faithful. If the Marcionites had been of Christ's sheep, they would surely have remained in the united doctrine and faith of the Church, which acknowledges the true humanity of Christ and knows nothing of the fiction of a phantastic body. Because they did not do this, it is clear that they were not true faithful of Christ. The same must be said of those who today dare to deny the doctrine of the gospel. Nor will it help the Papists that they profess Christ, that under the pretext of Christ they force all their own inventions upon us, that they boast of succession from the Apostles. For if they were of us, that is, of the true flock of Christ, they would surely remain with us, and would not depart from the doctrine of the Apostles, which teaches that we are justified by faith alone in Christ, without the works of the law. But since they dare to ascribe to the works of human traditions what the Apostles constantly denied to the works of the law divinely handed down, they cannot be of the Apostles and their lawful successors. Likewise, if they were of the faithful of Christ, they would remain with us in that faith and doctrine which teaches that Jesus Christ is the one mediator between God and men, and they would not, turning aside from it, devise new and countless mediators. If they were of the Church of Christ, they would by no means pervert the covenant of Christ which he himself instituted at the last supper, but would acknowledge it to be a remembrance of the Lord's death, and would not invent a repetition of the sacrifice offered by Christ. If they were of Christ's flock, they would hear the voice of Christ alone, and would not thrust human traditions, condemned by so grave a sentence of Christ, upon the Church, which strongly protests. Finally, if they were led by the Spirit of Christ, they would persist with steadfast faith in those things which have been handed down to us through Christ, and they would count accursed him who presumed to teach a new gospel, a new faith, a new way of salvation, whether he were an Apostle or an angel fallen from heaven. Gal. 1. Because they do not do this, but put forward the Fathers, Councils, Canons and other things of that kind, we shall confess that they are of the number of those on whose authority they rely, but we shall never acknowledge them to be of the flock of Christ's faithful. For if they were of us, they would surely have remained with us.

units.la: At quæråt aliquis, cur Deus ex ecclesia & eo coetu, qui Christi nomine insignitur, eiusmodi monstra & pestes prodire patiatur? Respodet Ioannes: Vt manifestum fiat, quòd non sint omnes ex nobis. Cautos vult reddere suos cultores dominus, ne facile & temere quibusuis fidant. Euangelij enim prædicatio sagenæ similis est, quæ tam putres quàm sanos pisces attrahit. Matth.13. Nam in orbe prædicatur inter eos qui varijs ducuntur affectibus, variè & diuersimodè recipitur. Et plures sunt, qui non gloriæ Dei & regni coelorum studio illud amplexantur, sed quòd illud suis studijs & priuatis cupiditatibus inseruire posse putant. Atqui horum conuersatio periculosa & incautioribus valdè noxia est. Adhibito igitur ventilabro dominus aream suam purgat, cogitationes & studia illorum retegit, ac permittit, vt absurdis opinionibus seipsos prodant, qui hactenus sub Christi nomine in ecclesiæ gremio delitescebant. Et cum illi reprobantur, qui electi sunt, probati fiunt.1. Cor.11. Neminem ergo offendat illorum hominum peruersitas. Prodest enim ecclesiam ab illis pestibus purgari, & illorum exemplo pios admoneri, vt caute salutem suam in timore & tremore operentur. Philip.2.
units.tr: But someone might ask: why does God allow such monsters and plagues to come forth from the Church and from that assembly which is named by the name of Christ? John answers: so that it may become plain that not all are of us. The Lord wishes to make his worshippers cautious, lest they trust readily and rashly in anyone at all. For the preaching of the gospel is like a net, which draws in rotten fish as well as sound ones. Matt. 13. For it is preached in the world among those who are moved by various affections, and it is received in various and diverse ways. And there are many who embrace it not from zeal for the glory of God and the kingdom of heaven, but because they think it can be made to serve their own studies and private desires. Yet the company of these men is dangerous and very harmful to the incautious. Therefore the Lord, with his winnowing fan, cleanses his threshing floor, lays bare the thoughts and aims of those men, and permits them, by their absurd opinions, to betray themselves, who until now lay hidden under the name of Christ in the bosom of the Church. And when those are rejected who are not chosen, those who are chosen are made manifest. 1 Cor. 11. Let no one, therefore, be offended by the perversity of those men. For it is profitable that the Church be purged of those plagues, and that the godly be warned by their example to work out their salvation cautiously in fear and trembling. Phil. 2.

units.la: Vidimus hucusquè fratres, quæ nouissimis diebus fidei & salutis pericula inferunt ex falsis doctoribus. Nec id Ioannis modò verba docent, sed illos iam multis locis, non sine multarum animarum iactura, grassari sentimus. Aperiamus ergo oculos metis nostræ, & vigilemus pro publica ecclesiæ salute. Vitemus & procul arceamus omnes, quotquot in simplici Christi doctrina & fidei vnitate nobiscum permanere nolunt. Audiamus verò & sequamur totis animis summi illius & fidelissimi pastoris, Iesu Christi vocem, cui debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in æternum. Amen.
units.tr: Hitherto, brethren, we have seen what dangers to faith and salvation false teachers bring in these last days. And not only do the words of John teach this, but we perceive that these men are now rampant in many places, not without great loss of souls. Let us therefore open the eyes of our mind, and watch for the public safety of the Church. Let us avoid, and drive far away, all who are unwilling to remain with us in the simple doctrine of Christ and the unity of the faith. But let us hear, and follow with all our hearts, the voice of that supreme and most faithful shepherd, Jesus Christ, to whom belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XII.
units.tr: Homily XII.

units.la: Et vos unctionē habetis à sancto illo, & nouistis omnia. Non scripsi vobis, quasi ignorantibus veritatem, sed tanquam scienti-bus eam. Et quod omne mendacium ex veritate non est. Quis est mendax, nisi is, qui negat Iesum esse Christum? Hic est Antichristus, qui negat patrem & filium. Quisquis negat filium, is nec patrem quidem habet.
units.tr: And you have the anointing from that Holy One, and you know all things. I have not written to you as to those ignorant of the truth, but as to those who know it. And every lie is not of the truth. Who is a liar, except he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son. Whoever denies the Son does not even have the Father.

units.la: Quamuis multa & varia sint, quæ hominis tam corpus quàm animam offendere possunt, nihil tamen tam noxium & pestilens est, quàm falsa doctrina, quæ Dei à verbo salutari ad vanas hominum traditiones abducit. Reliqua enim omnia fere eiusmodi sunt, vt pro noxijs agnosci, & proinde facilius caueri possint. At qui falsæ doctrinæ authores sunt, fere sub veritatis atque religionis specie imponunt, & salutem pollicentes, animabus interitum struunt. Quæ causa est, quòd tanto zelo falsos doctores passim in scripturis spiritus sanctus oppugnat, cuius testimonia non in prophetis modò, verùm etiam Dei filio videre licet, qui multis in locis cum his congreditur, & fideles, vt ab his sibi caveant, studiosè admonet. Imitatur tanti ducis exemplum discipulus ille Ioannes, qui (vt nuper vidimus) occasione à temporis circumstantia sumpta, paucis nos instituit de ijs, quæ hic obseruatu digna & necessaria sunt. Partim enim de magno illo Antichristo, partim verò de sui seculi impostoribus, loquens, docuit, vnde eiusmodi pestes ferè prodeant, quo signo agnosci possint, & cur tales ex suo cœtu emergere sinat dominus. Cæte-rum, quia admonitionum homines natura impatientes sunt, dum nec ignorantiæ nec negligentiæ insi-mulari volunt, Apostolus in præsenti studium suum excusat, ne qua suspicione cœpta admonitionē, alioqui necessariam, minoris facerent. Deinde ad institutum rediens, Antichristos, id est, doctores Christi æmulos siue aduersarios, duabus notis certis & infallibilibus describit, quo facilius agnosci & caueri possint.
units.tr: Although there are many and various things that can harm the body as well as the soul of a man, nothing is so harmful and pestilent as false doctrine, which leads men away from the saving Word to empty human traditions. For almost all other things are of such a kind that they can be recognised as harmful, and therefore more easily guarded against. But the authors of false doctrine mostly deceive under the appearance of truth and religion, and while promising salvation, they plot the destruction of souls. This is why the Holy Spirit so zealously attacks false teachers throughout the Scriptures, whose testimonies can be seen not only in the prophets but also in the Son of God himself, who in many places contends with them and diligently warns the faithful to be on their guard against them. The disciple John imitates the example of so great a leader, who (as we saw recently) taking occasion from the circumstances of the time, instructs us briefly about those things that are worthy of note and necessary here. For speaking partly of that great Antichrist and partly of the impostors of his own age, he taught whence such pests mostly arise, by what sign they can be recognised, and why the Lord allows such men to emerge from his own company. Moreover, because men are by nature impatient of admonitions, and do not wish to be accused either of ignorance or of negligence, the Apostle in the present passage excuses his own zeal, lest they should hold in less esteem an admonition begun with some suspicion, though otherwise necessary. Then, returning to his purpose, he describes the Antichrists, that is, the teachers who are rivals or opponents of Christ, by two certain and infallible marks, so that they may more easily be recognised and guarded against.

units.la: I. Et uos unctionem habetis à sancto illo, & nouistis omnia. Non scripsi uobis, quasi ignorantibus veri-tatem, sed tanquam scientibus eam. Vnctionem vocat internam institutionem spiritus sancti, quem Christus suis discipulis & omnibus, qui in se credunt, pollicitus est. Ioan. 14. & 16. Alludit autem ad typum veteris testamenti, quo reges & sacerdotes inungebantur, quæ unctio illos Deo sacros esse, & Dei spiritu regi debere docebat. At Christus, sacerdos noster & rex vnicus, non materiali oleo, sed (vt Psal. 45. habetur) oleo lætitiæ, ipso spiritu sancto, qui visibili specie super illum descendit (Ioan. 1.) inunctus, eam gratiam apud patrem meruit, vt eodem chrismate suos inungat, spiritum suum illis largiatur, illius inspiratione eosdem doceat & ducat in omne veritate, adeoq; sibi reges & sacerdotes consecret. Apoca. 1. Sic ergo vult Ioannes dicere: Nolim vos mea hæc ita accipere, o fratres, quasi vos tam crasse ignorantes & tam stupidè negligentes esse suspicer, qui hæc per omnia ignoretis, nec vlla admonitionum Christi, quas ille plurimas & fideles adhibuit, cura atque memoria tangamini. Scio enim vos, euangelij prædicatione iam olim institutos, salutis vestræ curâ agere. Scio vos, iuxta Christi promissionem, spiritus sancti chrisma accepisse, qui non modo salutis nostræ arrhabo est, nec modo de adoptione nostra, qua in filiorum Dei numerum suscepti sumus, testatur: verumetiam animos fidelium interna suggestione excitat, veritatis studium accendit, mentis oculos illuminat, vt falsum à vero discernere, & quæ saluti noxia sunt, cauere possint. Quia tamen variæ sunt hostis nostri satanæ artes, quibus errorum laqueos celare potest, & magna est etiam in sanctis interdum carnis ignauia, multisq; sæpius imposuit nimia securitas, externam institutionem vel viua voce vel scriptis adhibere, non superuacaneum, sed cum primis vtile & necessarium est. Sic Christus discipulos sæpe de ijsdem admonuit, & petres crebro inculcant, quæ liberorum saluti plurimum inseruire nouerunt.
units.tr: I. And you have the anointing from that Holy One, and you know all things. I have not written to you as to those ignorant of the truth, but as to those who know it. He calls the anointing the inward instruction of the Holy Spirit, which Christ promised to his disciples and to all who believe in him (John 14 and 16). He alludes, moreover, to the type of the Old Testament, by which kings and priests were anointed, which anointing taught that they were consecrated to God and ought to be ruled by the Spirit of God. But Christ, our priest and sole king, was anointed not with material oil but, as is said in Psalm 45, with the oil of gladness, by the Holy Spirit himself, who descended upon him in visible form (John 1). By being anointed he merited from the Father such grace that he anoints his own with the same chrism, bestows his Spirit upon them, teaches and leads them by his inspiration into all truth, and so consecrates them as his kings and priests (Rev. 1). So John wishes to say this: I would not have you take these words of mine in such a way, brethren, as if I suspected you to be so grossly ignorant and so stupidly negligent that you know nothing of these matters in full, and are not moved by any care or memory of the admonitions of Christ, which he gave in very many and faithful forms. For I know that you, instructed long ago by the preaching of the gospel, are concerned for your salvation. I know that you, according to Christ's promise, have received the chrism of the Holy Spirit, which is not only the pledge of our salvation, nor only bears witness concerning our adoption by which we have been received into the number of the sons of God, but also stirs the minds of the faithful by inward suggestion, kindles the desire for truth, enlightens the eyes of the mind, so that they may be able to discern the false from the true and to guard against what is harmful to salvation. Yet because the arts of our enemy Satan are various, by which he can hide the snares of error, and because there is also at times great sluggishness of the flesh even in the saints, and excessive security has often deceived many, it is not superfluous but especially useful and necessary to apply external instruction, whether by the living voice or by writings. Thus Christ often admonished the disciples about the same things, and the apostles repeatedly inculcate those things which they know to be most serviceable to the salvation of believers.

units.la: Docent & nos hæc Apostoli verba, non sufficere, si semel in veritate & salutis via instituamur, sed propter infinita pericula & carnis nostræ corruptione, crebris admonitionibus opus esse. Nam & iustus in die septies labitur. Prouer. 24. Et sponte quidem omnes labi possumus, proprijs autem viribus resurgere non possumus, sed tam interno spiritus motu, quàm institutione & admonitione externa opus est, quam Deus variis modis adhibet, plerunq; tamen per verbi ministe-rium: cuius curâ quicunq; commissam habent, non simpliciter modò prædicare vel docere, verum etiam (iuxta Pauli præceptum) arguere, increpare, exhortari, imò & tempestiuè & intempestiuè instare debent. 2. Tim. 4. Vani ergo illorum clamores sunt, qui doceri tantum volunt ex verbo Dei, ex eodem verò argui, moneri, & increpari non volunt. Ferunt illi indignissimè, si eadem crebrius inculcentur, & se ea plus millies audiuisse, & iá olim nouisse, clamitant. Quasi verò audiuis-se & nouisse sufficiat. Quoad factis non exprimitur, quod ex verbo Dei audiuimus, illud iterari, & maiori seueritate repeti, oportet.
units.tr: These words of the Apostle also teach us that it is not enough if we are once instructed in the truth and the way of salvation, but that because of the infinite dangers and the corruption of our flesh, frequent admonitions are needed. For a righteous man falls seven times a day (Prov. 24). Indeed, we can all fall of our own accord, but we cannot rise again by our own strength; therefore we need both the inward motion of the Spirit and outward instruction and admonition, which God applies in various ways, yet mostly through the ministry of the Word. Those to whom its care has been entrusted ought not simply to preach or teach, but also (according to the precept of Paul) to reprove, rebuke, exhort, and indeed to press on in season and out of season (2 Tim. 4). Vain, therefore, are the clamours of those who wish to be taught only from the Word of God, but do not wish to be reproved, admonished and rebuked from the same Word. They take it very ill if the same things are inculcated more often, and they cry out that they have heard them a thousand times and knew them long ago. As if hearing and knowing were enough! Unless what we have heard from the Word of God is put into practice, it must be repeated and urged again with greater severity.

units.la: Est autem diligenti obseruatione dignum, quòd Ioannes vnctionis, id est, internæ institutionis, quæ per spiritum sanctum fit, hoc loco meminit. Poterat enim vel aliorum Apostolorum, vel proprias, vel etiam ipsius Christi allegare, quas plurimas vbiq; habemus. Sed ostendere voluit, quis verus sit doctor fidelium. Vt enim homo proprij ingenij viribus non capit ea quæ sunt spiri-tus Dei (1.Cor.2.) ita nec is, quem spiritus illuminauit, quicquam suo studio & industria, sine spi-ritus operatione, in alterius mente ac intellectu efficere poterit. Institutum quidem est à Deo ver-bi ministerium, sed non vt propria dexteritate quicquā ministri faciant. Nihil enim est (inquit Pau-lus) qui plantat, nihil etiā qui rigat, sed Deus qui dat incrementū: Item: Quis Paulus? quis Apol-lo? nisi ministri, per quos credidistis, & vt cuiq; DOMINVS dedit? 1.Cor.3. Nisi ergo interna spiritus operatione illuminemur, trahamur & ducamur, nihil docentis vel eloquentia, vel indus-tria, vel eruditio proficiet. Ideo apud prophetā dominus de testamenti sui instauratione loquēs, ait: Dabo leges meas in mentem illorum, & in corde illorum ego inscribam illas. Iere. 31. Et alibi fi-deles suos omnes θεοδίδακτους, id est, diuinitus edoctos fore testatur. Ifa. 54. Ioan. 6.
units.tr: It is, moreover, worthy of careful observation that John here mentions the anointing, that is, the inward instruction, which is done by the Holy Spirit. For he could have cited either the other apostles, or his own writings, or even those of Christ himself, of which we have very many everywhere. But he wished to show who is the true teacher of the faithful. For just as a man by the powers of his own wit does not grasp the things that are of the Spirit of God (1 Cor. 2), so neither can he whom the Spirit has enlightened accomplish anything in another's mind and understanding by his own zeal and diligence, without the working of the Spirit. The ministry of the Word has indeed been instituted by God, but not so that ministers should accomplish anything by their own skill. For, says Paul, "neither is he that planteth anything, neither he that watereth, but God that giveth the increase." Likewise: "Who then is Paul, and who is Apollos, but ministers through whom you believed, and as the Lord gave to each?" (1 Cor. 3). Unless therefore we are enlightened, drawn and led by the inward working of the Spirit, the eloquence, industry or learning of the teacher will profit nothing. Therefore, speaking through the prophet of the renewal of his covenant, the Lord says: "I will put my laws into their mind, and I will write them upon their heart" (Jer. 31). And elsewhere he testifies that all his faithful will be θεοδίδακτοι, that is, taught of God (Isa. 54; John 6).

units.la: Arguunt hæc illorum insolentiam, qui humanæ rationi & sapientiæ tantū tribuunt, vt huius censuræ & iudicio religionis causam & controuersias de fide subijciant. Obstupescunt illi ad su-perbos scholarū titulos, quasi illorum authoritas valere debeat, qui per homines vel Magistri no-stri, vel Doctores facti sunt: cum maius sit multo spiritus sancti testimonium, quod fideles singu-li, cuiuscunq; loci & ordinis sunt, intra animum suum sentiunt. Illud ergo diligenter examinemus, & conferamus cum illis quæ scripturis tradita sunt, ne forsan contra Apostoli præceptum, homi-num serui reddamur, qui ab vnius Christi ore pendere debemus. 1.Cor.7. Cæterum ad Ioannem redeamus, qui & ipse ad institutum rediens, Antichristos certis notis describit.
units.tr: These things expose the insolence of those who attribute so much to human reason and wisdom that they subject the cause of religion and the controversies concerning faith to its judgement and decision. They are astonished at the proud titles of the schools, as if the authority of those should carry weight who have been made masters or teachers by men; whereas the testimony of the Holy Spirit, which each of the faithful, of whatever place and rank, feels within his own mind, is far greater. Let us therefore examine that diligently, and compare it with what has been handed down in the Scriptures, lest perhaps, contrary to the Apostle's precept, we become servants of men, when we ought to hang upon the mouth of Christ alone (1 Cor. 7). But let us return to John, who, returning himself to his purpose, describes the Antichrists by certain marks.

units.la: CAPVT II.
units.tr: CHAPTER II.

units.la: II. Et quòd omne mendacium ex veritate non est. Quis est mendax, nisi is, qui negat Iesum esse Chriſtum? Hic est Antichristus, qui negat patrem & filium. Quisquis negat filium, is ne patrem quidem habet. Possunt ex his duæ Antichristi notæ constitui, quarum altera fit. Mendacem vel à veritate alienum esse: altera vero, Negare patrem & filium. Sed de singulis ordine erit dicendum. In priori, ali qua ex contextu verborum siue constructione difficultas est, quæ magna ex parte tolletur, si sci-endi verbum, quo ante vsus erat, huc quoque transferas. Coniunguntur enim hæc ijs quæ præ-cesserunt, ad hunc modum: Scripsi vobis, non quasi ignorantibus veritatem, sed tanquam scienti bus eam. Vobis (inquam) scribo, qui scitis, quòd omne mendacium ex veritate non est. Videtur autem rem ipsam pro persona posuisse, mendacium nimirum pro mendace. Ex veritate non esse, pro eo posuit, quod est veritati contrarium & hostem esse, quod Antichristi proprium est. Qua-re forma argumenti hæc erit. Quicũque mendax est, ex veritate non est. Omnis, qui negat Iesum esse Christum, mendax est. Ergo, qui negat Iesum esse Christum, ex veritate non est, & per conse-quens, Antichristus est. Minorem vero non simplici orationis silo proponit, sed interrogationem amplificat, quasi dicat: Ecquis mędax dici poterit, si qui Iesum negat esse Christum, mendax non est? Imò hoc omnis mendacij caput, adeoq; summum & maximum inter omnia mendacia cense-ri debet: quia per hoc ipsissima & essentialis veritas negatur, nimirum Dei filius, Iesus Christus. Sunt autem in his duo obseruanda.
units.tr: II. And that every lie is not of the truth. Who is a liar, but he who denies that Jesus is the Christ? This is the Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son. Whoever denies the Son, the same has not the Father either. From these words two marks of Antichrist can be established: the first, that he is a liar or alien to the truth; the second, that he denies the Father and the Son. But each must be discussed in order. In the first there is a certain difficulty arising from the context and construction of the words, which will be largely removed if you carry over here the verb of knowing that he used before. For these things are joined to what preceded in this way: "I have written to you, not as those who are ignorant of the truth, but as those who know it." I write to you, I say, who know that every lie is not of the truth. He seems to have put the thing itself for the person, namely "lie" for "liar." "Not of the truth" he put for that which is contrary to the truth and its enemy, which is proper to Antichrists. Hence the form of the argument will be this: whoever is a liar is not of the truth; everyone who denies that Jesus is the Christ is a liar; therefore whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ is not of the truth and, consequently, is Antichrist. But the minor premise he does not state as a plain assertion; he amplifies it by a question, as if he were saying: "Could anyone be called a liar if he who denies that Jesus is the Christ is not a liar?" Indeed, this should be regarded as the head of every lie, and so the chief and greatest of all lies, because by it the very and essential truth is denied, namely the Son of God, Jesus Christ. Now there are two things to be observed in these words.

units.la: Primum, quid sit Iesum negare esse Christum. De Christi vocabulo iam ante dictum est, & alibi quoq; dicetur. Comprehendit hoc filij Dei pro nobis incarnati officium, quod in regno & sa-cerdotio administrando versatur. Docet autem scriptura, & iuxta huius traditionem fatetur & uniuersalis fidelium ecclesia, filium Dei in mundum venisse, vt fidi regis instar pugnam pro no-bis contra satanam hostem subiret, nos ex eius tyrannide assereret, inque nos regia liberalitate re-gni cœlorum thesauros profunderet. Fatetur præterea, eúdem sacerdotis quoque officio funĉtú esse, & fungi in æternum. Nam & olim docuit, & docet hodie per verbum suum. Deinde vt olim pro nobis orauit, ita hodie pro nobis intercessorem & aduocatum agit coram patre. Vnica ité cor-poris & sanguinis sui victima in ara Crucis immolata totius humani generis peccatum expiauit: quæ expiatio cum perfecta fit, & virtute sui meriti in æternum durét, iterationem nullam postu-lat. Hæc quicunque iuxta scripturas credunt, & cum uniuersali fidelium cœtu fatentur, ij Iesum hunc Christum esse fatentur. Omnis verò, qui ista in Christo agnoscere nó vult, Iesum hùc Chri-stum esse negat, & proinde vel Antichristus, vel magni illius Antichristi membrum dici meretur. Peccant igitur hoc loco, quicunq; Dei filium non vnum & solum saluatorem esse agnoscunt, sed quæ ad eius siue sacerdotium siue regnum pertinent, alió transferunt. Qui (inquam) alios deos tutelares inuocare, aliunde regni cœlorum thesauros petere, alios vitæ magistros sectari, alijs in-tercessoribus niti, alias satisfactiones amplecti, & noua sacrificia pro peccatis offerre docet. Faten-tur quidem Iesum esse Dei filiũ, & eundem Christi cognomine appellant. Sed quid prodest no-men tribuisse, si rem quæ nomine significatur neges? Si gemmæ smaragdi vim inesse neges, non-ne smaragdum esse negauisti? Nega radici inesse rapunticæ vim, & simul rapunticam esse negaue-ris. Frustra ergo verbis Christum fatentur, quicunq; quæ Christi sunt & ad eius officium perti-nent, negare audent. Negant autem, quicunq; eadem alibi quærunt vel monstrant, eò quod Iesus vnicus & solus saluator est, nec quenquam in suæ gloriæ consortium admittit. Act. 4. Isa. 42. Pec-cant & offenduntad eundem lapidem, qui doctrinam de Christo vnico saluatore contemnút, & nouis traditionibus illam farcire conantur. Et quia Christiani nominis professio non verba tan-tum, verum vitam & omnem vitæ conuersationem exigit, Christū negare dicuntur, quicunque impurè, impiè & slagitiosè viuunt, quod nunquà factúri erant, si pretioso Christi sanguine se ablu-tos & redemptos esse ex animo crederent. Ex hoc hominum genere sunt blasphemi, immisericor-des, contemptores verbi, impuri scortatores, impoenitentes adulteri, sanguinarij milites, & quicun-que sceleribus ita sese addixerunt, vt illa pro sceleribus non agnoscant, & multò minus depoeni-tentia cogitêt. Hæc si ad nostri seculi homines applicemus, facilé cernetur, quàm magna Antichri-stianorum turba sit, qui Iesum Christum tam doctrina quàm totius vitæ conuersatione abnegát. Et tamen adhuc, quis nam magnus ille Antichristus sit, dubij hæremus?
units.tr: First, what it means to deny that Jesus is the Christ. The name "Christ" has already been discussed, and will be discussed again elsewhere. The title covers the office of the Son of God, made flesh for us, which consists in the administration of the kingdom and the priesthood. Scripture teaches, and the universal church of the faithful confesses in accordance with this teaching, that the Son of God came into the world to fight for us against Satan, the enemy, as a faithful king would, to rescue us from his tyranny, and to pour out upon us, with royal generosity, the treasures of the kingdom of heaven. It further confesses that he performs the office of priest and exercises it for ever. For he both taught formerly and teaches today through his word. Then, just as he once prayed for us, so today he acts as our intercessor and advocate before the Father. The one sacrifice of his body and blood, offered on the altar of the Cross, expiated the sin of the whole human race; and since this expiation is complete and remains for ever by the power of his merit, it admits of no repetition. Whoever believes these things according to the Scriptures, and confesses them with the whole assembly of the faithful, confesses that this Jesus is the Christ. But whoever is unwilling to acknowledge these things in Christ denies that Jesus is the Christ, and therefore deserves to be called either Antichrist or a member of that great Antichrist. Those therefore sin in this matter who acknowledge the Son of God as the one and only Saviour, but transfer to others what belongs to his priesthood or his kingdom. I mean those who teach that one should invoke other guardian gods, seek the treasures of the kingdom of heaven elsewhere, follow other masters of life, rely on other intercessors, embrace other satisfactions, and offer new sacrifices for sins. They indeed confess that Jesus is the Son of God, and they even call him by the name Christ. But what good is it to have given him the name, if you deny the thing the name signifies? If you deny that a gem has the power of an emerald, have you not denied that it is an emerald? Deny that the root of the rapunculus has its power, and at the same time you will have denied that it is rapunculus. Therefore those who dare to deny what belongs to Christ and pertains to his office confess Christ in vain with their words. They deny him, however, whoever seeks or points to these things elsewhere, because Jesus is the only and sole Saviour and admits no one to the fellowship of his glory. (Acts 4; Isa. 42.) They also sin and stumble over the same stone, who despise the doctrine of Christ as the only Saviour and try to stuff it with new traditions. And since the profession of the Christian name demands not only words but life and the whole conduct of life, those are said to deny Christ who live impurely, impiously and shamefully, which they would never do if they sincerely believed that they had been washed and redeemed by the precious blood of Christ. To this class of people belong the blasphemers, the merciless, the despisers of the Word, the impure fornicators, the unrepentant adulterers, the bloodthirsty soldiers, and all who have so given themselves over to crimes that they do not recognise those things as crimes, and much less think of repentance. If we apply these things to the people of our own age, it will easily be seen how great is the crowd of Antichrists who renounce Jesus Christ both in doctrine and in the whole conduct of their lives. And yet we still hesitate: who that great Antichrist is?

units.la: Alterum hoc loco obseruandū est, quòd Antichristo mendacio tribuit, vt quod illi maximè proprium sit. Vt enim Christus Iesus ipsa est veritas, & irrefragabilis veritatis doctor: ita Antichri-stus totus mendacijs scatet, & ex mendacijs totum Antichristi regnū atq; ecclesia conflatur. Huc pertinet quòd Christus & Apostoli deceptione iniustitiæ & signa mendacia illi tribuût. Matt. 24. 2. Thess. 2. Licet enim quædam verè fiant, falsa tamen & mendacia dici merentur, quia non nisi in eum finem fiunt, vt homines à veritate abstrahant. Norunt hoc quicunque miracula, quæ olim
units.tr: The second thing to be observed here is that he attributes to Antichrist falsehood, as that which is most proper to him. For just as Christ Jesus is truth itself and the teacher of irrefutable truth, so Antichrist is wholly full of lies, and the whole kingdom and church of Antichrist is built up out of lies. To this belongs the fact that Christ and the Apostles ascribe to him deceptive unrighteousness and lying signs. (Matt. 24; 2 Thess. 2.) For although some of these things are truly done, they nevertheless deserve to be called false and lying, because they are done only for the purpose of drawing men away from the truth. Whoever has seen the miracles that were once

units.la: apud imagines & in monasterijs edita sunt, viderunt: quorum plerag; palàm falsa fuisse, sæpe deprehensum fuit: & si quid vnquam verè factũ est, totum hoc diabolicæ illusionis opus erat, in hunc finem factum, vt contra Dei præceptum imaginibus vota nuncuparent homines, imaginibus saluandi virtutem tribuerent, imagines colerent, totiq; ab illorum cultu penderent. Eadem totius doctrinæ, quæ in Papatu prædicatur ratio est. Nam contra Dei verbum liberi arbitrij vires, iustitiæ opera & merita homini tribuunt, quæ omnia cum scripturæ negent, non potest non salsissimum esse quod illi tradunt. Similiter contra Christi verbum, ijs, qui laborant & onerati sunt, in proprijs vel aliorum meritis pacem & requiem pollicentur, quæ promissio vtique est salsissima & manifeste mendax. Item contra æternæ veritatis verbum, nouos, & infinitos quidem, intercessores nobis apud Deum esse tradunt: Christi sacrificium per Missam iterari, sicq; viuis & mortuis applicari oportere contendunt: purgatorium fingunt, indulgentias Romanas vendunt, ad limina Petri & Pauli inuitant, salutem certis locis & temporibus astringunt, & innumera alia docent à veritatis verbo alienissima. Quin relicto Dei verbo humanas traditiones ecclesijs sub prætextu veritatis obtrudere non verentur. Si enim totum illud Ceremoniarum Chaos consyderes, nihil in illo diuinitus præceptum, nihil à Christo institutum, nihil ab Apostolis traditum, nihil scriptu rarum authoritate confirmatum videbis. Et cũ authores horum omniũ nominent, tempora quo que quibus illa multis demum seculis post Apostolis instituta sunt, dissimulare non possint, adhuc tamen eam, quæ verbo Dei debetur, authoritatem illis vendicare nõ erubescunt. Quòd si per sonas[?], quæ totum illud regnum administrant, inspiciamus, nil nisi vana nomina & mendaces titulos videbimus. Caput ecclesiæ dici vult, qui nec corpori totius ecclesiæ præsens adesse, nec vitalem spiritum in illius singula membra trâsfundere potest. Idem Christi vicarium sese profitetur, cum Christus, qui ecclesiam suam non deserit vnquam, vicario minimè opus habeat. Eiusdem farinæ est serui seruorum titulus, cum constet illum potius regem regum & dominum dominantium dici debere. Eadem est in huius capitis tam egregijs membris ratio. Episcopi dicuntur, qui nihil minus quàm episcopi sunt, si illos ad Pauli doctrinam & regulam examines, cum nec doceant nec etiam docere posint, & plerique vel in aulis principum, vel in legationibus obeundis versentur, ecclesias vero suas nunquam, aut saltem rarissimè inuisant. Ita monachi à solitudine dicũtur, qui turmatim in medijs vrbibus habitant, imò in aulis apud reges & imperatores non extremum locum tenent, sæpe etiam in castris inter signa militaria inueniuntur. Vouent illi paupertatem voluntariam, sed hoc titulo totius mundi opes sibi vendicant, & ad summos honores ascendunt. Vouent obedientiam, cum interim obedientiæ, quæ magistratui, parentibus & ipsi Deo debetur, iugum omnino excutiant. Vouent castitatem, sed eam præstant, qua alienis thoris insidiantur, qua virgines quasuis, etiam Deo sacras, violant, qua deniq; totum fere orbem stupris & spurijs repleuerunt. Profitentur se mundo mortuos, cum nemo magis in mundo viuat, nec alij spiritu mundi, qui odiorum, simultatum, ambitionis & inuidiæ author est, magis exagitentur. Hæc cum ita sint, nonne mendaces esse fatebimur? At si mendaces sunt, ex veritate non sunt, imò veritati se planè contrarios, & proinde Antichristos esse produnt. Sequatur ergo hos, si cui sordet veritas, & mendaciorum laqueis se scientem & volentem implicari gaudet.
units.tr: performed at images and in monasteries knows this: most of them have been shown to be plainly false, and if anything was ever truly done, the whole of it was a work of diabolical illusion, done for this end: that men should make vows to images contrary to God's command, should attribute to images the power of saving, should worship images, and should depend entirely on their worship. The same reasoning applies to the whole doctrine that is preached in Papistry. For against God's Word they attribute to man the powers of free will, works of righteousness and merits; since Scripture denies all these things, what they teach cannot but be most false. Likewise, against the word of Christ, they promise peace and rest to those who labour and are burdened, in their own or others' merits; this promise is surely most false and manifestly lying. Likewise, against the word of eternal truth, they teach that there are new and indeed countless intercessors for us before God; they contend that the sacrifice of Christ is to be repeated through the Mass, and so applied to the living and the dead; they invent a purgatory, sell Roman indulgences, invite people to the thresholds of Peter and Paul, bind salvation to certain places and times, and teach innumerable other things most alien to the word of truth. Indeed, having abandoned the Word of God, they do not hesitate to thrust human traditions upon the churches under the pretext of truth. For if you survey that whole chaos of ceremonies, you will see nothing in it commanded by God, nothing instituted by Christ, nothing handed down by the Apostles, nothing confirmed by the authority of Scripture. And although they name the authors of all these things, they cannot conceal that those things were instituted many centuries after the Apostles, yet they still are not ashamed to claim for them that authority which is due to the Word of God. But if we examine the persons who administer that whole kingdom, we will see nothing but empty names and lying titles. He wishes to be called head of the church, who can neither be present to the body of the whole church nor pour vital spirit into its individual members. He professes himself the vicar of Christ, although Christ, who never forsakes his church, has no need at all of a vicar. Of the same kind is the title "servant of servants", since it is agreed that he ought rather to be called King of kings and Lord of lords. The same is true of the members of this head, who are so excellent. They are called bishops, who are by no means bishops, if you examine them by the doctrine and rule of Paul, since they neither teach nor are able to teach, and most of them spend their time in the courts of princes or on embassies, and seldom or never visit their own churches. Thus monks are called solitaries, though they live in crowds in the middle of cities; indeed, in the courts of kings and emperors they hold no lowly place, and often they are even found in camps among military standards. They vow voluntary poverty, but under this title they claim for themselves the riches of the whole world, and they rise to the highest honours. They vow obedience, while at the same time they wholly shake off the yoke of obedience owed to the magistrate, to parents and to God himself. They vow chastity, but they practise the kind that lies in wait for other men's beds, that violates virgins of every sort, even those dedicated to God, and that has in the end filled almost the whole world with debauchery and bastards. They profess to be dead to the world, though no one lives more in the world, and no others are more driven by the spirit of the world, which is the author of hatreds, quarrels, ambition and envy. Since these things are so, shall we not confess that they are liars? But if they are liars, they are not of the truth; indeed, they plainly show themselves to be opposed to the truth, and therefore to be Antichrists. Let whoever despises the truth follow them, and let him rejoice to be knowingly and willingly entangled in the snares of lies.

units.la: Alteram Antichristi notam his verbis Apostolus describit: Hic est Antichristus, qui negat patrem & filium. Quisquis negat filium, is ne patrem quidem habet. Leuiculum videri poterat quod dixit, Antichristum esse, qui negat Iesum esse Christum. Addit ergo quod grauius est, & ab Antichristo non filium modò, sed etiam patrem abnegari dicit. At quis (ais) tam impius est, vt Deum negare ausit absolutè? Certè inter gentes Deos negare capitale fuit, & inter hæreticos nemo vnquam inuentus est, qui Deum patrem dissentis verbis negauerit. Hodie quoq; Iudæi & Turcæ, licet à Christo alieni, imò in illum blasphemi sint & impij, Deum tamen cœli ac terræ conditorem agnoscunt, & illius cultu fideq; in illum gloriantur. Probat ergo Ioannes quod dixit, & docet, sine Christi cognitione & fide in Christum, Dei patris cognitionem & cultum constare non posse. Qui filium (inquit) negat, is ne patrem quidem habet. Cohærent enim pater & filius, nec vllo modo separari possunt. Nam ea est inter filium & patrem relatio, vt altero sublato, alter quoque necessariò tollatur. Si enim pater est, filium habeat oportet, cuius pater dici queat. Sed & filius nemo dicitur, nisi patris respectu, è quo progenitus est. Accedit his, quòd essentialiter inter se cohærent Deus pater & filius, iuxta illud Christi: Ego & pater vnum sumus. Ioan.10. Item: Qui vidit me, vidit patrem meum. Credite mihi, quòd ego in patre sum, & pater in me. Ioan.14. Nec alium Deum scripturæ diuinitus inspiratæ tradunt, quàm eum, qui filiû habet ab æterno ex se genitum, quem præfinito tempore emisit in mundum, hominem factum ex muliere, & legi obnoxium, vt eos qui legi erant obnoxij, redimeret, &c. Gal.4. Quisquis ergo Dei filium, & quae is propter nos in carne gesit, negat: idem & Deum illum negat, qui scripturis sacris traditur. Recte ergo Ioannes colligit: Quisquis negat filium, is ne patrem quidem habet. At filium multiuariam negari, & inter Christiani nominis professores huius abnegationem esse plus satis vulgarem, supra daemonstrauimus. Non est ergo, quod vel Ioannis sententiam iniquiorem & duriorem aequo, vel eos nimios & vehementiores esse putemus, qui hodie Christi gloriam constanter asserunt, & Antichristum magno zelo oppugnant.
units.tr: The Apostle describes another mark of Antichrist in these words: "This is Antichrist, who denies the Father and the Son. Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father either" (1 John 2:22-23). It might seem a trifling thing that he said Antichrist is one who denies that Jesus is the Christ. But he adds something more serious: that Antichrist denies not only the Son but also the Father. "But who," someone may say, "is so impious as to dare to deny God outright?" Certainly among the nations to deny the gods was a capital offence, and among heretics no one has ever been found who denied God the Father in so many words. Even today the Jews and the Turks, although they are alien to Christ, and indeed blasphemous and impious against him, nevertheless acknowledge God as the creator of heaven and earth, and boast of their worship of him and their faith in him. John therefore proves what he has said, and teaches that without knowledge of Christ and faith in Christ, the knowledge and worship of God the Father cannot stand. "Whoever denies the Son," he says, "does not have the Father either." For the Father and the Son are bound together and cannot in any way be separated. The relation between Son and Father is such that if the one is taken away, the other is necessarily taken away too. For if there is a Father, he must have a Son of whom he can be called Father; and no one is called Son except in respect of the Father from whom he was begotten. Add to this that God the Father and the Son are essentially bound to each other, according to the saying of Christ: "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30); likewise: "He who has seen me has seen my Father. Believe me, that I am in the Father and the Father in me" (John 14:9-10). Nor do the Scriptures, divinely inspired, hand down any other God than the one who has a Son begotten from himself from eternity, whom in the appointed time he sent into the world, made of a woman and subject to the law, to redeem those who were under the law, etc. (Gal. 4:4-5). Whoever therefore denies the Son of God, and what he did for us in the flesh, also denies that God who is delivered to us in the holy Scriptures. John therefore rightly concludes: "Whoever denies the Son does not have the Father either." But that the Son is denied in many ways, and that this denial is more than common among those who profess the Christian name, we have shown above. There is therefore no reason to think that either John's judgment is more unfair and harsh than it should be, or that those are too excessive and vehement who today steadfastly assert the glory of Christ and oppose Antichrist with great zeal.

units.la: Arguuntur autem hoc dicto omnes omnium gentium religiones, quae extra Christum institutae sunt, & viam salutis aliam monstrant, quam quae in Christo nobis propositam est. Glorientur, vt libet, de Deo patre & creatore omnium rerum, tam Iudaei quam Turcae, cum filium non habeant, patre illos carere necesse est. Praetexant alij zelum suum pium & sanctum, nec hic tamen quicquam iuuare poterit. Nec enim nostri animi & zeli placitis Deus coli vult, sed iuxta regulas abs se nobis praescriptas & traditas. Non peruestigetis (inquit) post cor vestrum, aut post oculos vestros, post quos scortari soletis. Quin memores estote, & facite omnia praecepta mea, & fitis sancti Deo vestro. Num 15. Et Christus ait: Nemo venit ad patrem, nisi per me. Ioan. 14. Nisi ergo per Christum, qui via vnica & sola est, ad thronum gratiae & in Dei commercium tendamus, frustra in aliis cultibus occupabimur. Non leues itaque sunt, o fratres, nostri seculi de religione & fide Christiana controuersiae, nec de verbis pauculis contenditur. De summa rerum & capite fidei contenditur, dum nos solum Christum retinere, soli omnem redemptionis gloriam tribuere volumus, aduersarij vero infinita alia illi coniungere audent, sine quibus salutem nos consequi posse negant. At quia Christus gloriae suae consortem ferre nequit, in gloriam ipsius peccant, imo Christum abnegant, quicunque quae illius sunt, vel in seipsos, vel alias Creaturas transferunt. A Christo autem excidere non possumus, nisi nos ipso patre & gratia patris in vniuersum spoliemus. Horum itaque memores non sine graui cura & solicitudine expendamus fidei negotium, induamus feruentem Christi zelum, abominemur Antichristi tyrannidem, suspecta habeamus quaecunque Christi merito aliqua ex parte detrahere videntur, & ab eius solius voce pendeamus, cui soli debetur benedictio, honor, gloria & potestas in aeternum. Amen.
units.tr: Now by this saying all the religions of all nations that have been established outside Christ, and that point to a way of salvation other than the one set before us in Christ, are refuted. Let the Jews and the Turks boast as they please of God the Father and creator of all things; since they do not have the Son, they must necessarily lack the Father. Let others pretend that their zeal is pious and holy; yet this will avail nothing here. For God does not wish to be worshipped according to the pleasure of our minds and zeal, but according to the rules prescribed and handed down by him to us. "Do not seek out," he says, "after your own heart or after your eyes, after which you are accustomed to play the harlot. Rather, remember and do all my commandments, and be holy to your God" (Num. 15:39-40). And Christ says: "No one comes to the Father except through me" (John 14:6). Unless, therefore, we strive through Christ, who is the one and only way, toward the throne of grace and into communion with God, we shall labour in vain in other worships. The controversies of our age concerning religion and the Christian faith are therefore not trivial, nor is the dispute about a few words. The dispute concerns the sum of things and the chief point of faith, since we wish to retain Christ alone and to ascribe all the glory of redemption to him alone, while our adversaries dare to join countless other things to him, without which they deny that we can obtain salvation. But since Christ cannot bear a sharer in his glory, those who transfer to themselves or to other creatures what belongs to him sin against his glory, indeed deny Christ. We cannot fall away from Christ unless we strip ourselves entirely of the Father himself and of the grace of the Father. Mindful of these things, let us therefore weigh the matter of faith not without serious care and anxiety; let us put on the fervent zeal of Christ, abhor the tyranny of Antichrist, hold suspect whatever seems in any way to detract from the merit of Christ, and depend upon the voice of him alone, to whom alone belong blessing, honour, glory and power for ever. Amen.

units.la: HOMILIA XIII.
units.tr: HOMILIA XIII.

units.la: Vos igitur quod audiuistis ab initio, in uobis maneat. Si in uobis manserit quod audiuistis ab initio, & uos in filio & patre manebitis. Et haec est repromissio, quam ipse pollicitus est nobis, uitam aeternam. Haec scripsi uobis de his, qui seducunt uos.
units.tr: Therefore, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you. If what you have heard from the beginning remains in you, you also will remain in the Son and in the Father. And this is the promise which he himself has made to us: eternal life. I have written these things to you concerning those who lead you astray.

units.la: Dominus & saluator noster Iesus Christus in euangelio ait: Nemo, qui manu aratro admota respexerit a tergo, idoneus est regno Dei. Luc.9. Praeclara omnino & grauis sententia, dignaq; quam omnes pij perpetuo ob oculos habeant. Docet enim, non sufficere, vt Christi cognitionem semel assequamur, & fidem in hunc profiteamur aliquandiu, sed fidei constantiam requiri, quain finem vsque perseueremus. Atqui hic nobis duo fere negotium faciunt, mundus nimirum & falsa doctrina. Vt enim ille vitiorum illecebris animos tentat, & a puritate vel innocentia vitae abstrahit: ita falsae traditiones sub pietatis praetextu, fidei & religionis veritati insidiantur, & vbi admissae fuerint, fidem & religionem omnem euertunt. De vtroq; igitur magna diligentia Ioannes agit: singulari tamen zelo contra falsam doctrinam & doctores Antichristianos disputat, quos in ijs, quae praecesserunt, docet non leuiter impingere, sed in praecipuo fidei & religionis capite errare, cum & Iesum Christum & patrem omnino abnegent: quod in eum finem dicit, vt maius in nobis excitet hos deuitandi studium. Postquam vero illos sufficienter descripsit, breuem institutionem subiungit, qua primum quid fideles facere debeant, docet: deinde fructus & praemia amplaconsilio suo obtemperantibus pollicetur, de periculo rursus illos admonens, ne frustra tamen haec agere videatur.
units.tr: Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ says in the Gospel: "No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God." Luke 9. This is a truly outstanding and weighty saying, and one that all the godly ought to keep constantly before their eyes. For it teaches that it is not enough to come to know Christ once and to profess faith in him for a while; constancy of faith is required, so that we persevere to the end. Yet two things almost always make this task difficult for us: the world, to be sure, and false doctrine. For just as the world tempts minds with the allurements of vices and draws them away from purity or innocence of life, so false traditions, under the pretext of piety, lie in wait for the truth of faith and of religion, and once they have been admitted, they overturn all faith and all religion. John therefore deals with both with great care, yet he argues with particular zeal against false doctrine and Antichristian teachers. He teaches that those whom he has described in what went before do not stumble lightly, but err in the chief point of faith and religion, since they utterly deny both Jesus Christ and the Father. He says this with the aim of stirring up in us a greater eagerness to avoid them. After he has sufficiently described them, however, he adds a brief instruction, in which he first teaches what the faithful ought to do; then he promises fruits and great rewards to those who obey his counsel, warning them again of danger, lest he seem to be doing this in vain.

units.la: Vos igitur quod audiuistis ab initio, in uobis maneat. Est haec praesentis loci propositio, quae breue quidem praeceptum completitur, tale vero, quod contra omne erroris & seductionis periculum nos praemunire potest. Respondetur eodem hoc omnium quaestionibus, qui quid hodie inter tot tamq; graues de fidei & religionis doctrina controuersias fieri debeat, interrogant. Dicit enim Apostolus: Quod ab initio audiuistis, in vobis maneat. Quasi dicat: Ut ut illi noua quotidie excogitent, vobis tamen nouis doctrinis atq; praeceptis minimè opus est. Ab initio enim tradita sunt ecclesiae quaecunq; ad hominum salutem sunt necessaria. Ea vos retinere conuenit, & in illis perseuerare constantibus animis, sicq; nullum erit ex Antichristis periculum. Loquitur autem de simplici salutis doctrina, quae à prima mundi origine reuelata, & paulatim magis magisq; illustrata est, donec absoluto per Christum redemptionis nostrae negotio, Apostoli illam per totum orbem inter omnes gentes praedicarunt. In ea igitur perseuerent, quicunq; inter nostri seculi controuersias salutis iacturam facere nolunt. Debet autem huius praecepti eo maior penes nos esse authoritas, quod & alibi nobis praescribitur. Nam & Christus Iesus, cum varia nouissimi seculi pericula, quae tam ex falsis doctrinis, quam aliunde fidelibus accident, exposuisset, constantia in agnita veritate, ceu unicum aduersus mala haec omnia remedium, commendat, dicens: Qui perseuerauerit usque in finem, saluus erit. Matth. 24. Paulus item de seductoribus Timotheum admonens, ait: Tu perfistito in his, quae didicisti, & quae tibi concredita sunt, sciens à quo didiceris, & quod à puero sacras literas noueris, quae te possunt eruditum reddere ad salutem per fidem, quae est in Christo Iesu.2.Timoth.3. Turpissimè[?] ergo falluntur, qui hodie, propter diuersas de fide doctrinas, nouo quodam docendi genere opus esse exiistimant, & ad conciliationes quasdam conuersi eiusmodi doctrinae formam constituere conantur, quae ab omnibus recipi & ferri possit, modo pertinaces esse desinant. Quia enim circa fidem varia & diuersa dogmata seminari, & homines in discordes sententias scindi videmus, ideo constantia fidei & agnitae veritatis perseveranti atque pertinaci studio opus est. Nec enim nostri iuris est Dei verbum, ut quae illo traduntur, pro nostro arbitrio mutare, & ad hominum placita formare liceat. Caeterum quia ad eam doctrinam relegat Ioannes quae ab initio statim tradita, & per Apostolos cum ecclesiae congregarentur praedicata est, operae-pretium erit, eam summatim comprehensam inspicere, ut ceu in speculo videamus, quid nobis hodie ample&tendum, quidue vitandum sit.
units.tr: "Therefore, let what you have heard from the beginning remain in you." This is the proposition of the present passage, which, though it is a brief precept, is of such a kind that it can fortify us against every danger of error and seduction. The same answer is given to all those who ask what ought to be done today amid so many and such grave controversies over the doctrine of faith and religion. For the Apostle says: "What you have heard from the beginning, let it remain in you." As if he were saying: however those men may devise new things every day, you have no need at all of new doctrines and precepts. For from the beginning there were handed down to the Church all those things that are necessary for the salvation of men.
